column4: a dark back room drawn in pixels, a round table under one low lamp; every figure, chair, the cylinder and the icons are drawn in code, none an emoji or a bare circle
the room does fall into dark past the lamp's pool (corners of the shot); whether it reads as held-breath tension is a feel line, for the person's play
480x270 canvas scaled by whole numbers only (PIXEL, index.html:32); the shot shows the fixed view from above and a little to the side
six block figures with squared shoulders; the table and the cylinder are round (evidence/play.png)
the cylinder's chambers, the faces and the brackets on my own chamber are the brightest things; wall and floor stay in a narrow dark range

amber lamp and the name of whoever's turn it is, crimson live rounds and the danger line, teal empty chambers, ink-navy room, bone text; the night past the pool is blue and the pool is tinted amber (drawLight, index.html:715)
eyes, beard, glasses, hands and lettered chambers carry the detail; the wall, floor and rug are large flat areas (evidence/play.png)
one pixel size throughout; every figure is rectangles with a one-pixel ink outline pass (drawRects) and one shadow tone on the side away from the lamp; seen in evidence/figures.png

drawLight dithers an amber pool and the night round it; lampPos (index.html:734) swings it and tickTable (index.html:590) leans it to the seat acting; in evidence/play.png it sits towards the top seat, whose turn it is. The swing itself is motion a still does not show
the rules section (newGame, applyAction, viewFor, volley) is the page's nine rules; the name, room, figures, cylinder and layout are this game's own (evidence/play.png)
2D, one fixed view; nothing in the code moves the camera except the shake on a shot

applyAction: 16 credits, looks 1 and 2, turns 3 and 4, hidden deposits of 1 to 3 towards 6 with the excess lost, then the swap; advance (index.html:164) moves the lead and passes seats with no credits; three seats out ends it; volley (index.html:234) fires from the muzzle's seat clockwise. Numbers in config.js. Played to the end in evidence/results.png

six seats and six lettered chambers, the muzzle on the rim; a pair is picked with the left and right keys or the mouse (updateHuman, index.html:519; marks in drawOverlays, index.html:911); a turn of the muzzle is animated (ringAngle, index.html:670)

the title's bot level line; each bot waits before it acts (goTurn, index.html:433; the dots beside the top seat in evidence/play.png); slips are botSlip (index.html:291); every bot's name ends in the word for bot
pale-rimmed chambers everyone has seen, amber ticks on the ones only I know or can work out, closed ones unknown, a key for both in the panel, and the line for my own chamber with brackets round it
one line per action in the panel, an amber bar on the lines since my last move, and an icon beside each head for what that seat last did

one shot a seat with the word on the table, smoke and the chair down; evidence/results.png is the results screen with R for a new game (index.html:1172). The warning with two seats out is a log line (index.html:475), the red count and a pulse (index.html:605): the pulse is sound, not heard by any check

six figures, each its own outline, in the pixel room (evidence/play.png); sounds are built in sfx (index.html:116) and M mutes (index.html:93). No check listens: how they sound is for the person's play
none of the page's nine rules is changed; their numbers are config.js lines 9 to 17
bot level chosen on the title (index.html:1128); Enter starts the seat draw, where the six appear one by one with their seat numbers (index.html:1146); seated in evidence/play.png

the panel shows my credits, 16 at the start (15 after one look in evidence/play.png); as I sit down the lamp leans to my seat and my name turns amber (tickTable, index.html:590; drawLabels, index.html:883). No still of the draw itself is kept
the log reads round 1, lead Moru, then Moru's move on one line; bots wait in goTurn (index.html:433)
five buttons with their costs; my public look at A and B opened both and logged what was in them

on that first look the line for my chamber turned to live and the brackets round it went red; a 1 turn costs 3 and hands the chamber to the next seat (applyAction, index.html:174), carried out by the person's keys in a scripted game

when the first real trouble comes depends on the play. In the seeded first game a live round faces the person's seat from the start, found on the first look; nobody timed when the first turns of the muzzle came
one pool of credits pays for looks, turns and deposits (applyAction, index.html:174); botAct turns the muzzle away from a round it knows of: a bot's turn is in the log of evidence/volley.png
the log shows the third seat running out and the volley starting at once (applyAction ends the game there, index.html:174)
the screen says eliminated, and R or Enter starts a new game (index.html:1172)

normal bots slip (botSlip; Moru's first move in evidence/play.png is one); expert bots weigh what others' moves suggest (suspicion, index.html:246) and count how close the end is (botAct, index.html:301). Whether that feels like people is for the person's play
